PullRequest.Title: Modern UI: align status bar and activity bar icons
PullRequest.Body: ## Summary - Align the outer status bar icons with the activity bar icon column in both Modern UI layout densities, including the compact activity bar size. - Mirror the horizontal inset on the right, preserve the hidden-activity-bar fallback, and keep colored and joined edge items consistently padded. - Add layout regression coverage for both densities, both activity bar sizes, and standard, colored, and joined edge items. No linked issue was supplied. ## Issues addressed | Severity | Issue | Resolution | |---|---|---| | UI | Status bar edge icons drift from the activity bar icon column, and compact-density edge spacing is asymmetric. | Match the inset to the activity bar lane in each density and use symmetric edge-label padding on both sides. | Additional actionable findings from the final code review: None. ## Validation | Command | Result | |---|---| | `npm run transpile-client` | Passed after updating the branch to current `main`. | | `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts --reporter dot` | Passed: 94 tests. | | `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/browser/media/floatingPanels.css` | Passed. | | `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts` | Passed. | | `git diff --check` | Passed. | | `npm run -s precommit` | Passed through the normal commit hook, including hygiene checks. | Live Code OSS measurements also confirmed zero icon-centre offset on both status bar edges in default and compact densities, with the activity bar positioned on either the left or the right. Environment limitations: the regular client build helper in the existing checkout encountered a pre-existing Copilot SDK/runtime version mismatch before compilation. Direct client transpilation passed. An independent baseline client build using `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` passed; its broader dependency bootstrap encountered registry authentication `E401` in extension setup. The visual checks therefore used isolated profiles with extensions disabled. No registry or authentication configuration was changed. ## Visual evidence **Manual image upload pending.** The requested before/after images have been captured locally; the author chose to upload them manually. This PR remains a draft until the images are attached and verified. Both runs use macOS Code OSS Dev, Dark 2026, a 1440 × 900 CSS-pixel viewport, the same small sample workspace and isolated profile, and disabled extensions. Each image combines identical crops of the left activity/status bar and the far-right status bar; full-window originals were retained. The baseline ran in a detached worktree at `7c4967fad97`; its affected visual sources are unchanged in the latest `main`. The temporary baseline worktree and evidence-only windows were removed after capture. ### Default density | Before | After | |---|---| | Upload `before-default-edges.png` here. | Upload `after-default-edges.png` here. | ### Compact density | Before | After | |---|---| | Upload `before-compact-edges.png` here. | Upload `after-compact-edges.png` here. | Measured offsets relative to the activity icon column: | Density | Before: left / right | After: left / right | |---|---|---| | Default | -4px / -4px | 0px / 0px | | Compact | -4px / -2px | 0px / 0px | To check manually, enable Modern UI and switch **Layout Density** between **Default** and **Compact**. Confirm that the first status bar icon centres under the activity icons, the rightmost status bar icon has the matching edge inset, and colored/joined items retain their expected hover surfaces. Also check the compact activity bar size and a hidden activity bar. ## Review status - Unresolved actionable findings: None. - Residual risks: live extension-contributed edge items were not exercised; the regression tests cover the corresponding standard, colored, and joined item classes. Image attachment and remote CI verification are pending.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or update the Modern UI status bar with standard, colored, or joined edge entries
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browser matches the changed static selectors during normal style recalculation and lays out the status bar before paint. No JavaScript measurement or asynchronous work was added to the production render path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total status-bar entries can vary, but the effective matched cardinality for each edge selector is at most two entries. Entry visibility changes already recompute first/last markers across the collection; this diff does not alter that loop or its frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser style calculation and layout remain serialized on the renderer main thread; the diff adds no tasks, queues, promises, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The stylesheet is loaded through the existing workbench CSS path. Cold startup parses the same stylesheet with a few simplified rules; warm status-bar updates reuse the parsed stylesheet. There are no application caches, cache keys, misses, retries, or coalescing changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff only changes padding declarations and broadens existing edge rules from colored edge items to all edge items; statusbarModel proves only the edge entries receive these marker classes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style-recalculation duration depends on status-bar size and browser state, but matching remains root-scoped and the changed edge selectors can affect only the first visible left entry and last visible right entry.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The CSS changes alter geometry for a constant number of nodes without introducing forced measurements, broad invalidation primitives such as :has or class-substring selectors, or additional layout passes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle Modern UI density, compact activity-bar size, or activity-bar visibility
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing root-class mutation invalidates styles and triggers the required workbench relayout; the changed rules then select one status-bar container and its two edge labels. That existing relayout remains the only work required before the new layout is visible.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One status-bar container and at most two edge labels per workbench window, independent of editor count, workspace size, or extension count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Class updates and subsequent style/layout work execute synchronously on the renderer main thread. The diff introduces no repeated scheduler, listener, or concurrent burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both density variants are already present in the loaded stylesheet, so toggling uses warm parsed CSS. No network, filesystem, IPC, subprocess, database, or cache lookup is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: activitybarPart mirrors compact state onto the existing root class, and the changed rules only consume those existing state classes; no mutation path was added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost of a full workbench relayout varies by open UI, but that relayout pre-existed because these settings already change layout metrics. The diff adds only constant-scope status-bar declaration changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR changes resulting padding values and selector specificity but does not increase toggle frequency, layout cardinality, or boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the Modern UI browser layout regression suite
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added test constructs a small fixed DOM and performs synchronous getBoundingClientRect measurements after class changes; those style/layout flushes are on the test's critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed at four configurations and three variants over two status-bar icons and one activity icon; it does not scale with repository or user data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Measurements run serially in one test. Four density/activity-bar configurations each measure three fixed edge-item variants; there is no unbounded loop or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The test uses the already imported CSS and in-memory DOM. Browser style data is warm after initial setup; there are no cache misses or external operations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added test directly contains the class writes and geometry reads, and is confined to test code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual headless-browser layout times vary, but the DOM and iteration count are fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable product performance regression. Although the test intentionally forces bounded synchronous layouts to verify geometry, it runs only in the browser test suite and has constant cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and every diff hunk. Checked CSS invalidation scope, status-bar marker ownership and multiplicity, density/activity-bar toggle lifecycle, synchronous layout reads in the new test, and all transitive external boundaries. No high-confidence actionable performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.
